characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Sample prepared by standard metallographic grinding and coarse/fine polishing, then etched with 2 % Nital solution (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10–15 s
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain the microstructural image of the homogenized/water-quenched M1 (M1-HQ) sample

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Systematic addition of Al to the Fe–8Mn-0.2C system; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; equilibrium phase fractions and austenite composition evaluated as a function of temperature, yielding a predicted ICT range of 600–900 °C and equilibrium austenite fraction of ~50 % at the selected IAT of 700 °C for M1.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C (M1) ingot fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of the raw materials throughout the ingot. This precedes homogenization and yields the as-cast precursor of M1-HQ.
Homogenization of the as-cast M1 sample at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this condition is designated M1-HQ in Table 1 and is the state of the present sample.

structures.overall_structure: Water-quenched (homogenized) condition of the Si-free alloy M1 (M1-HQ); optical micrograph shows lath/needle-like martensitic contrast.

unmapped_findings: M1-HQ is the homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching) condition of the Si-free alloy M1 (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C); the paper's detailed microstructural characterization (SEM/EBSD), XRD phase quantification and uniaxial tensile testing were carried out on the hot-rolled (M1-HR) and intercritically annealed (M1-IA) conditions rather than on M1-HQ, so no tensile, hardness or quantitative phase-fraction data are reported specifically for M1-HQ.

Per Table 1, the M1 (3Al-0Si) sample naming convention is M1-AC (as cast), M1-HQ (homogenized, 1100 °C/2 h + water quenching), M1-HR (hot rolled, ~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C) and M1-IA (intercritically annealed, 700 °C/1 h + water quenching); M1-HQ was an intermediate processing state shared by both steels (M1-HQ and M2-HQ).
